maria-support: Hey @acme-dev — saw your escalation about intermittent 500s and auth errors. Can you paste the latest request-id(s) you saw and a minimal snippet you used to call the API?

acme-dev: Hi — thanks. We see spikes and occasional 403/500 combos. Last seen: request-id=42f8c9b2 and request-id=42f8c9d0. Using our Node SDK in prod. Can't share full app, so here's a trimmed down example that reproduces ~30% of the time locally.

acme-dev: ```js
// node minimal
const Redwood = require('@redwood/inference');
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.RW_KEY });
(async () => {
  const res = await client.generate({ model: 'redwood-1.0', input: 'Hello', max_tokens: 16 });
  console.log(res);
})();
```

maria-support: thanks — can you also run a curl that shows the response headers? we need the exact request-id header value the backend returned. Example curl below — run with your same token and paste stdout/stderr.

maria-support: ```bash
curl -v -sS -D - \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Hello","max_tokens":8}'
```

tim-oncall: if you get a 500 include the response body and the headers block. Also run it with `-w "\\n_HTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\\n"` appended so we capture HTTP code in the same output.

acme-dev: ran it once — here's output (sanitized):

acme-dev: ```
< HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error
< Date: Wed, 08 Jul 2026 14:21:02 GMT
< request-id: 42f8c9b2
< content-type: application/json
{"error":"internal","message":"runtime oom"}
_HTTP_CODE:500
```

dev-aaron: thanks, that's very helpful. Two quick asks: 1) can you run the same call but add the header `x-rw-trace: capture` so our runtime will include extra trace info in logs; 2) please capture a debug bundle via the small script below (this zips up env, last 200 lines of your client logs, and the curl output).

dev-aaron: curl with trace header:

dev-aaron: ```bash
curl -v -sS -D - \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $RW_KEY" \
  -H "x-rw-trace: capture" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-1.0","input":"Hello","max_tokens":8}' -w "\\n_HTTP_CODE:%{http_code}\\n"
```

dev-aaron: debug bundle script (run from your workstation):

dev-aaron: ```bash
#!/bin/bash
set -e
OUT=redwood-debug-$(date +%s).tgz
mkdir -p /tmp/rwdebug
cp /var/log/myapp.log /tmp/rwdebug/ || true
tail -n 200 /var/log/myapp.log > /tmp/rwdebug/client_tail.log || true
env | grep -E 'RW_|REDWOOD_' > /tmp/rwdebug/env.txt || true
# include the curl stdout saved to /tmp/rwdebug/curl_output.txt if you run with -o
if [ -f /tmp/rwdebug/curl_output.txt ]; then mv /tmp/rwdebug/curl_output.txt /tmp/rwdebug/curl_response.json; fi
tar -czf $OUT -C /tmp rwdebug
echo $OUT
```

maria-support: when you have the tgz, upload it to the secure upload link I DMed you (one-time). Please also include the two request-ids you pasted.

acme-dev: OK will run with the trace header and the script. Quick question: is there a minimal Python + Go example we can try so our infra tests both SDKs? We want identical calls.

dev-aaron: python minimal:

dev-aaron: ```py
# python minimal
from redwood import Redwood
c = Redwood(api_key="$RW_KEY")
print(c.generate(model="redwood-1.0", input="Hello", max_tokens=8))
```

dev-aaron: go minimal:

dev-aaron: ```go
// go minimal
package main
import (
  "fmt"
  rw "github.com/redwood/inference-go"
)
func main(){
  client := rw.NewClient("$RW_KEY")
  resp, _ := client.Generate(rw.GenerateRequest{Model:"redwood-1.0", Input:"Hello", MaxTokens:8})
  fmt.Println(resp)
}
```

maria-support: perfect — when you send the debug bundle I'll triage logs and escalate to runtime team if we see OOMs. If you still hit 500s after the trace header, paste the exact request-id and we can correlate immediately.

acme-dev: uploaded redwood-debug-171235.tgz to your DM link. included curl_output.txt and client_tail.log. The two failing ids: 42f8c9b2, 42f8c9d0.

maria-support: got the bundle, thanks. I'm kicking off correlation. ETA ~20–30m. If we need a short repro with a smaller prompt that deterministically triggers the issue, we'll ask — for now the trace header + request-ids are ideal.
